acceptanceCriteria.statement: Only an authenticated owner, project manager, or project member with active project access may create a card in an active column of a board in that project; viewer, outsider, sibling-project grant, revoked grant, missing board/column, or archived/read-only ancestry cannot create or infer private data.

Creation accepts title trimmed to 1–200 characters, valid nullable Gregorian date-only deadline, one of five priorities, and zero to 20 distinct active eligible project assignees; malformed values and unknown fields are rejected with stable validation responses, not silently stripped/coerced.

The expected board version and active-column condition are checked atomically with the insert, ordering, activity and idempotency receipt; same-key same-command retries return the original outcome without a second card, while key reuse with a different command conflicts.

Board list returns only active authorized cards in canonical rank order; each compact summary has accurate title, priority, due date, assignee IDs, position, version, comment count and finalized-image count without description/history, and counts/filter totals reflect the complete matching set rather than only the page.

Authorized detail reads return the complete active card and only eligible/historical person display records; unknown, trashed, purged and cross-project IDs resolve privately without body, email, count, or existence leakage.

Field update requires an active authorized card and expected version; only supplied fields change, title/description limits hold, and stale versions return 409 with no partial field/history/receipt effects.

All five priorities and null or real Gregorian YYYY-MM-DD deadlines are accepted; impossible dates such as 2026-02-30, timestamp substitutions and malformed formats are rejected. Due dates remain calendar dates without timezone shifts.

Zero or multiple assignees are allowed up to 20, only active eligible owner/manager/member identities in the same project may be newly assigned, duplicates and unknown/removed/sibling identities fail atomically, and removed historical identities remain safely displayable where required.

Move validates active destination column and same-board neighbor IDs, neighbor adjacency/full canonical destination order, card and board versions, and current project write authority; rank, card version, history/activity and receipt commit atomically or none do.

Concurrent moves/edits use database transaction locks or equivalent serialization and return canonical positions; stale competing requests produce a recoverable conflict rather than duplicate ranks, lost updates, partial events, or corrupt ordering.

Placement lookup is bounded and authorized, returns canonical full-column first/last/before/after choices and required versions, and rejects missing, foreign, stale, trashed, or ineligible placement references.

Filtered results/counts are project-scoped and exclude trash. Movement placement is calculated against full destination ordering rather than a filtered subset; ambiguous filtered drag is not represented as a server-backed safe operation.

Concurrent field edits and moves use expected card/board versions; stale updates return 409 and perform no partial effects; DB-level parallel requests, not only sequential calls, establish the result.

Idempotency receipts are actor/project/method/resource scoped, hash the semantically complete request, are reauthorized against current access before replay, and same-key concurrent requests produce one logical effect and one consistent outcome.

Card field Save changes only fields; comments and image uploads remain independent commands. Backend side effects and receipts are atomic; a lost response/retry does not duplicate a logical effect. Draft preservation, dialog recovery and actual browser behavior are UI acceptance and remain explicitly unverified by backend evidence.

Mounted Node and Worker routes use the same intended PostgreSQL, auth/session, project ancestry and write-lock paths as tested. Authenticated identity is never derived from client-supplied actor headers; request bodies, queries, response contracts and database rows have no unknown-field or schema drift.

Migrations and constraints preserve workspace/project/board/card ancestry, active assignment integrity, versions/order uniqueness where specified, activity and receipt relationships; actual PostgreSQL tests exercise isolated synthetic two-project data and concurrent requests.
